original_question: Let lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3 be distinct supersingular values of lambda, where the elliptic curve branched at {0, 1, infinity, lambda} is supersingular. For the hyperelliptic curve branched at {0, 1, infinity, lambda_1, lambda_2, lambda_3}, which of the group schemes (Z/p + mu_p)^2, M + (Z/p + mu_p), N, or M^2 can occur as its p-torsion? Here M denotes the unique p-torsion group scheme of a supersingular elliptic curve.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Question 4.3 of the Glass-Pries note Questions on p-torsion of hyperelliptic curves within arXiv:math/0411059
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact open problem. It uses the same branch locus {0,1,∞,λ1,λ2,λ3}, the same notion of a supersingular value λ, and the same four candidate p-torsion group schemes. It also correctly identifies M as the unique p-torsion group scheme of a supersingular elliptic curve.
missing_details: The ambient field should be stated: k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, and from Section 3 onward the paper assumes p > 2.
The paper is asking about the p-torsion of the Jacobian, i.e. Jac(X)[p], not literally a p-torsion group attached to the curve X itself.
The hyperelliptic curve should be identified as the smooth genus-2 double cover X → P^1_k branched exactly at {0,1,∞,λ1,λ2,λ3}.
N must be defined: it is the p-torsion group scheme of a supersingular abelian surface that is not superspecial.
The quantifier should be explicit: among all triples of distinct supersingular values λ1, λ2, λ3, which of the four isomorphism classes actually arise as Jac(X)[p]?

If one wants the stand-alone question to be nonvacuous, one should either assume that three distinct supersingular values exist or note that this forces p >= 7, since the paper says there are (p-1)/2 supersingular values of λ.

The paper asks only an occurrence question up to isomorphism of finite commutative group schemes; it does not broaden this to a full classification by p-rank, a-number, or larger moduli-theoretic strata.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 2. Let M denote the unique isomorphism class of the p-torsion group scheme of a supersingular elliptic curve over k, and let N denote the p-torsion group scheme of a supersingular abelian surface that is not superspecial. Suppose λ1, λ2, λ3 are distinct supersingular values in k, meaning that for each i the elliptic curve branched at {0,1,∞,λ_i} is supersingular. If X is the smooth genus-2 hyperelliptic curve X → P^1_k branched exactly at {0,1,∞,λ1,λ2,λ3}, then, as the triple (λ1, λ2, λ3) varies over all such distinct supersingular triples, which of the four group schemes (Z/p ⊕ μ_p)^2, M ⊕ (Z/p ⊕ μ_p), N, and M^2 can occur, up to isomorphism, as the Jacobian p-torsion group scheme Jac(X)[p]?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of the paper's actual open problem, namely Section 4, Question 4.3. The surrounding paragraph introduces it as the simplest case relevant to strengthening Corollary 3.5 so as to obtain hyperelliptic curves with a-number exactly 3. Section 2 supplies the meanings of M and N, and Section 3 supplies the standing assumption p > 2 for the remainder of the note. I therefore kept the scope exactly on the occurrence of the four named group schemes as Jac(X)[p] for the genus-2 hyperelliptic curve branched at {0,1,∞,λ1,λ2,λ3}, and only made explicit the ambient field, the Jacobian, the genus, and the quantifier over all distinct supersingular triples.
